articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of White-Light Absorption Efficiency in Multi-Dimensional Perovskites
abstract: This research aims to comprehensively analyze three distinct perovskite materials, two-dimensional perovskite (2DP) (BA2MA3Pb4I13), traditional three-dimensional perovskite, MAPbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> (3DP), and CS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.05</inf> FA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.79</inf> MA<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.16</inf> PbI<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2.45</inf> Br<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.55</inf>, also known as triple cation, mixed halide perovskite (3DP-TC). The primary emphasis is on examining their interaction with incoming broadband radiation, including towards photovoltaic (PV) technology. Our investigation begins with a thorough examination of the optoelectronic properties of these perovskite materials when used as photo absorbers in an n-i-p architecture for PV devices. To enhance our understanding, we conduct surface analysis on freshly synthesized perovskite films by employing various material characterization techniques for a comparative assessment using techniques such as photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy and scanning electron microscopy (SEM). We also explore the efficiencies of the three perovskite absorbers when they are integrated into PV architectures. The scope of this paper is an insightful demonstration into the potential of these three classes of perovskites spanning dimensionality from 3D to 2D within the crystalline unit cell, for shedding insights on their optoelectronic behavior, and their performance in PV applications.

articleTitle: Prediction of Household Energy Usage via Multi-Head Attention
abstract: The analysis of spatial and temporal information has been a task commonly accomplished through traditional statistics and signal processing, however with the information typically possessing nonlinear characteristics, the usage of machine learning based approaches has increased due to their ability to analysis data with high nonlinearity. Long Short Term Memory (LSTM), a type of Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), have shown to be favored due to their internal memory allowing the network to process data in a sequence of steps due to its feedback connections propagating predicted information back multiple times. We propose a neural network algorithm utilizing a modified Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with incorporated LSTM layers and multi-head attention to predict spatio-temporal data with higher metric performance compared to current state of the art networks, when each network is trained and tested on energy data of a single household.

articleTitle: Toward a Cost-Effective Smart Crop Health Monitoring System
abstract: In this research we have investigated and imple-mented smart-connected and cost-effective technologies that can aid with the crop management. In particular, we have installed nodes with various sensors in several parts of a Green house to supervise environmental and lighting conditions as well as to monitor the growth of plants. Furthermore, the overall monitoring system further includes a central access node for accumulating the sensory data that can also be accessed remotely for further analysis. The data collected from this research will be used in determining the optimal placement of sensors within the Green house, their performance as well as the strategies to be followed for minimizing the growth rate of plannts while at the same time maximizing their health. Finally, we have integrated all sensors input data into a Graphical User Interface.

articleTitle: Perovskite Solar Cell Degradation Driven by Collector Electrode and Prototypical Demonstration for Low-Power Electronics
abstract: Powering the Internet of Things (IoT) with renewable, efficient, and green energy sources is a critical and growing need in today's world. Solar power as a renewable energy source has the potential to significantly boost the expansion of the IoT ecosystem. And the remarkable increase in Power Conversion Efficiency (PCE) associated with perovskite solar cells, with PCE surpassing 25% has garnered a high interest in fueling the IoT expansion. However, the enduring stability of perovskite solar cells under operational conditions and environmental storage remains a central challenge for their successful commercialization and needs to be addressed for successfully using them in low-power electronics for IoT. The perovskite solar cell is formed using multiple layers and failure of a single layer causes the entire cell's performance to be compromised. Here we report on the degradation of perovskite solar cells driven by the choice of the common electrodes (Ag and Au). In this report, we have conducted a comprehensive analysis on the impact of pinholes of the hole collector layer with Au and Ag electrodes for the degradation mechanism associated with two types of perovskites, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{MAPbI}_{3}$</tex> and a triple cation absorber, Cso. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{osFA}_{0.79}\text{MA}_{0.\iota}{}_{6}\mathrm{P}\text{bI}_{2.4}\text{sBr}0.5^{\underline{\mathrm{s}}}$</tex>. For material characterization we used photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, while for device measurements, we analyzed the PCE with environmental storage. Finally, a prototypical demonstration followed, where we used our array of fabricated cells to power up an external circuit validated by the illumination of a low-power LED. These solar cells open up avenues to incorporate such devices to power up the IoT.

articleTitle: Halide Grown Monolayer WSe2 with Al Contacts for Photodetection Using Broadband Light
abstract: Despite the fact that two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) have gained a lot of interest due to novel features they exhibit at low dimensions, continued research in these materials will enable some of the challenges to be addressed. High-quality 2D TMDC synthesis, understanding the dynamics of quantum many-body interactions in monolayer nanosheets, which affect optoelectronic properties, and the importance of metal-2D semiconductor interfaces for enabling high-performance devices are examples of a few such areas that continue to evolve with more research. In this work, we discuss the vapor-based synthesis of our high crystalline quality WSe2 process, where a WSe2 photodetector was then fabricated with Al contacts. From this effort, we measured a promising photoresponsivity for our <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}1/\text{WSe}2$</tex> device fabricated on <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}/\text{Si}$</tex> substrates. Our successful demonstration validates the tremendous potential of WSe2 to open avenues for state-of-the-art electronic, optoelectronic, and quantum-optoelectronic devices using scalable vapor-based synthesis processes.

articleTitle: Environmental Stability Study of Solution-Processed Black Phosphorus
abstract: As two-dimensional materials gain increased traction toward device applications, the need to expand on the material used proportionally increases. Black phosphorus (BP) is a notable two-dimensional material that exhibits favorable optical characteristics such as a bandgap tunable by the thickness of the material. Despite the favorable properties of the material, BP is highly susceptible to environmental conditions such as moisture and oxygen exposure. This shortcoming has stunted the growth of BP manufacture via additive manufacturing methods such as ink-jet printing with chemically exfoliated material. In this work, we fabricated graphene and BP electronic devices on silicon substrates via ink-jet printing and tested their stability when subjected to varying temperatures and ambient exposure times. To ensure the quality of the both devices, Raman spectroscopy was performed where both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{g}^{l}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$A_{g}^{2}$</tex> vibrational modes were observed in BP. To combat the onset of oxidative degradation, the BP device was coated with ionic liquids (ILs) as a passivation layer. Two-terminal I/V measurements were conducted at 0,6,24, and 48 hours to monitor current changes over a 48-hour period, as well as an 18-month test for graphene. We also tested the effects of temperature from 5 - 335 Kelvin for BP. Overall, this study demonstrates that passivating with ionic liquids is an effective avenue for more robust solution processed black phosphorus devices.

articleTitle: Excitonic and Plasmonic Interactions of Gold Nanoparticles with Vapor-Synthesized WSe2
abstract: Transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs) based photodetectors have unique optoelectronic properties. When the TMDCs are integrated with other material systems, such as lower dimensionality zero-dimensional (0D) entities, plasmonic effects with the metallic OD systems allow for the coupling to excitons in semiconducting TMDS. In this work, we discuss the excitonic and plasmonic coupling towards plexcitonic interactions in hybrid van der Waals structures composed of a 2D WSe2 membrane interacting with OD Au nanoparticles. Two geometries of the nanoparticles is analyzed, specifically the spherical (Au-Sp) and the bipyramidal (Au-BP) architectures. The use of ultraviolet-visible (UV-VIS) optical absorption spectroscopy allowed us to probe the behavior of the interactions for each of the two architectures. Photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy revealed the excitonic behavior in our vapor synthesized monolayer (1L) WSe2, as well as the Au-Sp/WSe2 and Au-BP/WSe2 hybrids. Our findings demonstrate that geometry-mediated response of the Au nanoparticles provides another degree of freedom to modulate the carrier photodynamics in WSe2, which can also be useful for tailoring the optoelectronic performance of the broader class of semiconducting 2D materials.

articleTitle: Characterization of Solution Processed and Mechanically Exfoliated $\text{WSe}_{2}$ Towards Gas Sensors
abstract: In this study, we conducted a preliminary analysis on the utilization of two-dimensional <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{WSe2}$</tex> for gas sensors. Our approach involved creating a chemically exfoliated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{WSe2}$</tex> device with gold (Au) electrodes to monitor its response to a specific gas, in this case, carbon dioxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{CO}_{2})$</tex>. The films were produced through solution processing and electrically connected in a two-terminal setup. To understand the film's properties, we employed various microscopy and spectroscopy techniques such as Raman and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy, and optical microscopy. This enabled us to confirm the film's structure and chemical characteristics as we proceeded to measure the electronic transport of the films when exposed to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CO}_{2}$</tex> gas. Our work serves as an initial step towards further investigating <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{WSe2}$</tex> as a gas-sensing material for low-power and miniaturized sensors, utilizing additive manufacturing techniques.

The ability to classify power quality disturbances is essential for grid stability across the world. Rapid advances in machine learning have allowed for the development of complex signal processing techniques to address this issue. This paper proposes three extremely efficient deep learning models to identify disturbances in power quality. Model EPQC prioritizes efficiency, Model Huge-EPQC emphasizes accuracy, and Model Large-EPQC combines accuracy with efficiency.

This paper introduces the OSCAR2023 model, designed for constrained applications where computational efficiency is paramount. OSCAR2023 considers compression ratio, image quality, and computational cost. It aims to achieve a delicate balance between compression performance and computational requirements, much like the simplicity and high compression rates that made JPEG dominant at the time.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Optimization and Validation with ST-Microelectronics X-Cube-AI
abstract: As artificial intelligence models continually expand in size and complexity, the deployment onto embedded mi-crocomputer systems becomes progressively more challenging. This paper provides an assessment of the AI integration tools furnished by ST-Microelectronics (STM) for ARM M4 and M7 development systems. The research performed shows that minor alterations to a machine learning models architecture can significantly impact X-Cube-AI's ability to compress and successfully deploy to a ST microcontroller while maintaining accuracy.

articleTitle: Efficient Vision Transformer Classification of COVID-19 in Chest X-Rays
abstract: This work introduces CoViT, an efficient transformer-based algorithm designed to identify COVID-19 patients through chest X-ray radiographs. CoViT aims to outperform existing solutions by achieving a balance between efficiency and accuracy, surpassing the capabilities of most professionals. While previous AI solutions for COVID-19 detection have shown promise, many are either resource-intensive, less accurate, or focus on more expensive and less accessible diagnostic imaging. CoViT is a promising tool for the efficient diagnosis of COVID-19 using readily available chest X-ray radiographs.
